program.welcome: Beginners, families, and experienced jugglers are all welcome
about: {name} is a juggling club for {area}: balls, clubs, and rings, plus flow arts like poi, staff, and hoop. We meet to learn patterns, pass with partners, and cheer each other on. {welcome}.
Never juggled? Working on five balls? This is your crew. {loaners} Someone will always help you with your first cascade.

pillars.title: Learn
pillars.text: Never juggled? Someone will teach you the three-ball cascade, one throw at a time.

pillars.title: Play
pillars.text: Passing patterns, juggling games, and open jams anyone can join.

pillars.title: Flow
pillars.text: Poi, staff, and hoop for anyone who'd rather spin than catch.

pillars.title: Share
pillars.text: Try clubs, rings, and other props, and trade tips on gear and patterns.

program.meetup_blurb: A free, drop-in juggling and flow arts meetup. Beginners welcome, loaner props available.
program.volunteer: We're run by volunteers. Help set up, greet first-timers, teach a trick, or plan an event. Every bit counts.
program.donate_text: Meetups are free, always. Donations cover loaner beanbags, clubs, practice poi, and venue costs.
program.contact_note: First time? You don't need to email first. Just show up. But we're happy to answer questions.

loaners.yes: We bring loaner beanbags, clubs, and practice poi to every meetup, so you don't need to bring anything.
loaners.no: Bring your props if you have them. No props? Three rolled-up pairs of socks will do to start.

cost.details: Meetups are free. No dues, no fees, no membership forms.

learn.title: Learn to Juggle
learn.intro: Juggling is mostly throwing. Good throws make easy catches. Start here, then come to a meetup and we'll help in person.

basics.title: One Ball
basics.text: Toss one ball from hand to hand in an arc that peaks about eye level. Get it smooth and even before adding another.

basics.title: Two-Ball Exchange
basics.text: Toss one. When it peaks, toss the other underneath it. Catch, catch, stop. That's the whole pattern in miniature.

basics.title: Three-Ball Cascade
basics.text: Start with two balls in your dominant hand. Keep throwing on each peak. Drops are part of it, so practice by a wall or a bed.

basics.title: Try Flow Props
basics.text: Poi, staff, and hoop are about smooth motion, not catches. Start slow, with soft practice poi or a light hoop.

learn.levels_intro: A rough order to learn things in. Skip around. Every pattern you learn counts.

levels.label: Level 3
levels.name: Flow & Further
levels.text: More objects, partners, and flow props.

learn.outro: Learning is faster in person. Bring your props and questions to the next meetup.

faq.a: {name} is a juggling and flow arts club for {area}. We bring together {players} {ages}, from first-timers to experienced players. {welcome}.
Not at all. Most people come to play, learn tricks, and have fun. Competing is up to you.

faq.q: When and where do you meet?
faq.a: {meetup}. We meet at {venue}, {address}. Come and go anytime during the meetup.
No. Just show up. If a meetup is ever cancelled, we post it on this site and our social media as early as we can.
Nothing. {loaners} Wear comfortable clothes you can move in.
Yes! All ages are welcome. Younger kids should come with a parent or guardian, especially the first time.

faq.q: Do I need to know how to play?
faq.a: No. Total beginners are just as welcome as experienced players. We'll teach you the cascade one throw at a time.
Three soft beanbags. They don't bounce or roll away, so practice goes faster. Try our loaner clubs and poi before you buy those.
Not to our meetups. Fire spinning needs its own space, safety gear, and the venue's permission. Bring practice props instead.

faq.q: How do I become a member?
faq.a: Just come to a meetup. There's no sign-up. If you show up, you're part of the club.
Yes, please. Email {email} or talk to us at a meetup. We always need help setting up, greeting newcomers, and running activities.

faq.q: Can my organization partner with the club?
faq.a: Yes. We're open to venue partnerships, demos, workshops, and sponsorships. Email {email} with your idea.

safety.title: Keeping Meetups Safe
points: Kids are welcome. Younger kids need a parent or guardian with them. A parent or guardian is responsible for their own child at every meetup.
Club volunteers never take kids anywhere away from the group or the meetup space.
Give each player a clear circle. Clubs, staffs, poi, and hoops need room, so check around you before you start.
Practice props only: no knives, torches, or fire at meetups. Watch ceilings and lights with high throws.
safety.photos: We sometimes take photos at meetups for this website and our social media. Tell a volunteer if you or your child would rather not be photographed. We never post a child's full name, and we take photos down whenever asked.

conduct.intro: {name} is built on the idea that juggling and flow arts should be fun and welcoming for everyone. That only works if people treat each other well. This code sets out what we expect from everyone in our community.
conduct.short: Be kind. Be welcoming. Don't make anyone feel unsafe or unwelcome. If you see something, say something.
applies: Everyone at our meetups and events, including players, parents, and spectators
Competitors and spectators at contests we run
Anyone in our online spaces and group chats
expected: Be respectful. Treat everyone with dignity, whatever their age, skill level, race, ethnicity, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, religion, or background.
Be welcoming, especially to beginners and younger players. Everyone was new once.
Keep feedback encouraging. If someone asks for tips, help. Skip the harsh criticism.
Mind the space. Keep the venue clean, watch your circle, and look out for kids.
Respect decisions. Raise disagreements with organizers calmly and privately.
unacceptable: Harassment of any kind, including unwanted contact, following, or persistent unwanted attention
Photographing someone who asked not to be photographed
Discrimination, slurs, or jokes that put people down
Threats or intimidation, in person or online
Taking or damaging someone's gear without permission
Disruptive behavior that ruins the meetup for others
equipment: Ask before you borrow someone's props, and hand them back the way you got them.
Look around before you spin or throw. Clubs, staffs, and poi need open space.
Practice props only: no knives, torches, or fire at meetups.
Return loaner props before you leave.
conduct.reporting: If something makes you uncomfortable, tell a club volunteer at the meetup or email us. We take every report seriously and keep it as private as we can.
conduct.consequences: Organizers may give a warning, ask someone to leave a meetup, or ban someone from future events, depending on what happened. For anything involving a child's safety, we will contact the venue and, where needed, the authorities.
